newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's first half overseas equity issues fall.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's first half overseas equity issues fall.

text.p: Overseas equity-linked securities issuances by South Korea's listed companies fell to $734.2 million in the first half of 1997 from $859.9 million a year earlier, the Securities Supervisory Board said on Wednesday.

A securities watchdog statement attributed the decline to falling overseas demand for South Korean issues and worsening conditions for South Korean borrowers following a slew of debt defaults by big domestic companies earlier this year.
However, Samsung Electronics issued its convertible bonds at a 74.13 percent premium and zero percent coupon rate.
Bonds issued by Medison Co carried a 0.25 percent coupon rate with a 40 percent premium.
Equity-linked securities by South Korea's listed companies usually have been issued with a premium due to the foreign stock ownership ceiling. The current limit was set at 23 percent.
Samsung Electronics became the first South Korean company to issue overseas equity-linked securities on December 19, 1985, with a $20 million convertible bond issue in the European market.
Since then, South Korean companies have issued an aggregate of $10.55 billion worth of overseas equity-linked securities by the end of the first half of 1997.
